title: Stochastic probe decoupling and warm-pool prioritization: action plan and playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
postmortem_summary: During intermittent capacity events in late Jan–Feb 2026 we observed repeated underprovisioning and noisy scale cycles on KEDA-backed queues. Root cause analysis shows the probe signal (percentile-based queue latency) was being biased by a small cohort of long-tail requests. This produced stochastic false positives where HPA/KEDA would trigger scale-ups that then immediately decayed when the noisy requests cleared, causing oscillatory provisioning and increased cold-starts for warm pools. Secondary contributors: aggressive warm-pool eviction heuristics and probe gating tied too tightly to single-metric percentiles.
impact_timeline: 2026-01-28 03:40 UTC: first signs of queue latency spikes in us-west-2; 2026-01-28 03:45 UTC: KEDA scales up 3x; 2026-01-28 03:50 UTC: traffic spike subsides but HPA remains elevated briefly then scales down; 2026-02-02 11:12 UTC: similar pattern observed during model rollout; 2026-02-14 06:00 UTC: customer-reported increased 95th percentile latency; 2026-02-18 17:30 UTC: mitigations (probe smoothing) deployed to staging for validation
root_cause: 1) Single-metric percentile probe is sensitive to outliers created by sporadic long requests (batching/large-context inference). 2) HPA/KEDA decision window is short and couples directly to instantaneous percentile results, amplifying noise. 3) Warm pool eviction policy does not prioritize instances that previously served high-tail requests, causing repeated cold-starts when new requests arrive.
detection_and_mitigation_notes: Alerting surfaced via synthetic load tests and on-call Slack. Initial mitigations included increasing probe window and enabling 99->95 smoothing which reduced oscillation but did not eliminate false positives. Canary rollout was blocked until warm-pool prioritization proof-of-concept validated.
tradeoffs_considered: Option A: increase probe aggregation window (reduces sensitivity, increases detection lag). Option B: implement statistical outlier filtering (complex but preserves responsiveness). Option C: prioritize warm-pool instances based on recent tail-serving history (adds state and bookkeeping). We selected a combined approach: moderate window increase + outlier filtering + warm-pool prioritization to balance latency SLOs versus provisioning noise.
action_items: (Owner: Marco) Implement probe decoupling: introduce dual-path probe where percentile signal is filtered through an outlier-detector (MAD-based) and a smoothed-percentile estimator. Target: merge PR by 2026-03-05.
(Owner: Priya Singh) Extend KEDA scaler to support voting over short windows (3s, 15s, 60s) and require consensus before hard scale decisions. Deliverable: API and tests by 2026-03-12.

(Owner: Diego Morales) Warm-pool prioritization: tag instances with recent-tail-served boolean and prefer them for new cold-start avoidance; expose metric to Console. Target: design doc by 2026-03-01, implementation by 2026-03-22.
(Owner: SRE team lead) Tune eviction policy to maintain a small cohort (configurable) of 'tail-ready' instances per AZ. Rollout: staged across regions starting 2026-03-10.
(Owner: QA) Add synthetic scenarios to CI that create sporadic long-tail requests to validate decoupling under load. Deadline: 2026-03-08.
(Owner: PM - Elena Park) Update runbook and alerting thresholds: create alert to detect oscillatory scale patterns and auto-open incident. Runbook update by 2026-03-11.
(Owner: Observability) Add dashboard panels for probe noise fraction, warm-pool retention, and scale-vote consensus metric. ETA: 2026-03-09.
(Owner: Security) Confirm no KMS/HSM impact for warm-pool tags and persistence. Review complete by 2026-03-05.

(Owner: Eng leadership) Schedule 2-week verification window post-rollout to measure reduction in scale oscillations and cold-starts; success criteria: 50% reduction in scale events per-hour and 30% reduction in 95th latency regressions versus baseline. Start: 2026-03-23.
(Owner: Documentation) Publish a developer-facing guide describing probe configuration knobs, tradeoffs, and templates for workload patterns. Target publish date: 2026-03-16.
follow_up_notes: We will run two concurrent experiments in staging: A) conservative smoothing only, B) decoupled probe + warm-pool prioritization. Collect metrics for 72 hours and compare oscillation frequency and latency SLO impact. Decision to ship combined approach will require clear evidence from experiment B.
review_feedback: Design review (2026-02-27): PM requested clearer rollback plan; SRE requested circuit-breaker to avoid sustained overscaling. Actioned: added vote thresholds and emergency disable flag. Security requested minimal instance metadata change — adopted warm-pool boolean only.
notes: This ticket is intended to be the canonical action plan for preventing stochastic probe-induced autoscaler oscillations. Keep updates succinct and add new sub-issues for large implementation tasks.
